selected_evidence.requirement: CA generated on node1 named 'OS Comparison Root CA', self-signed CA:TRUE
selected_evidence.summary: openssl genrsa + req created the CA key/cert; x509 -text output shows Subject=Issuer=CN=OS Comparison Root CA, O=OS Comparison and Basic Constraints CA:TRUE, confirming a valid self-signed root CA.

selected_evidence.requirement: CA certificate installed as a trusted system CA on node1
selected_evidence.summary: Copied cert to /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors and ran update-ca-trust extract; trust list shows the 'OS Comparison Root CA' label as a trusted certificate and openssl verify against the system ca-bundle.crt returns OK.

selected_evidence.requirement: End-to-end proof the trust store actually honors the new CA
selected_evidence.summary: Signed a test leaf certificate (CN=test.oscomparison.local) with the new CA and verified it against the system CA bundle; verification succeeded, proving real trust chain validation.
Captured boot_id (2fc81aed-3ce8-4a35-8f4c-b73206afa45f) and uptime start prior to reboot, alongside the already-verified healthy CA trust state (cmd-64c60eb8611c4875, cmd-b81cb513678d4b3a).

Backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' via nohup; command returned REBOOT_ACK immediately, confirmed by the subsequent poll hitting a connection timeout (cmd-ed2eceb86adb4edb), proving the node went down after acknowledging.

selected_evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proving a real restart occurred
selected_evidence.summary: First poll timed out (node down mid-reboot); second poll succeeded with boot_id 5019b2cf-a284-44c6-b89f-0a769741f070 (different from baseline 2fc81aed...) and a new uptime start of 2026-09-03 09:23:44, proving a genuine reboot.

selected_evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of the CA trust configuration on node1
selected_evidence.summary: After the reboot, trust list still shows 'OS Comparison Root CA', the anchor file is intact, and openssl verify against the system CA bundle still returns OK, confirming persistence across restart.
